favorites: Games you marked with X. A shortcut shelf for the titles you keep coming back to.
lastplayed: Recently launched games, newest first. Pick up where you left off without hunting the library.
arcade: Coin-op arcade hardware spanning decades of cabinets. Run MAME / FBNeo sets from a single shelf.
cps1: Capcom Play System I (1988). The board behind Final Fight, Street Fighter II, and other CPS classics.
cps2: Capcom Play System II (1993). Street Fighter Alpha, Marvel vs. Capcom, and the later CPS fighters.
neogeo: SNK Neo Geo AES/MVS. Home and arcade carts with the same 2D sprites, from Metal Slug to King of Fighters.
atari2600: Atari 2600 (1977). The VCS that brought cartridge games into living rooms — Combat, Pitfall, Adventure.
atari5200: Atari 5200 SuperSystem (1982). A 8-bit follow-up with analog sticks and ports of arcade hits.
atari7800: Atari 7800 ProSystem (1986). Backward compatible with many 2600 carts, plus arcade-style 7800 titles.
atarilynx: Atari Lynx (1989). Color handheld with hardware scaling and rotation — California Games, Chip's Challenge.
atarijaguar: Atari Jaguar (1993). 64-bit era console with a small, cult library including Tempest 2000 and Alien vs Predator.
atarist: Atari ST home computer. MIDI, demoscene, and 16-bit microcomputer software beyond consoles.
nes: Nintendo Entertainment System / Famicom. The 8-bit console that defined platformers, RPGs, and licensed arcade ports.
snes: Super Nintendo Entertainment System / Super Famicom. Mode 7, rich palettes, and the 16-bit Nintendo library.
n64: Nintendo 64. Analog stick, four controller ports, and 3D Nintendo / Rare / Acclaim cartridges.
gb: Game Boy (1988). Green-screen handheld that made Tetris and portable Nintendo a worldwide habit.
gbc: Game Boy Color (1998). Backward compatible with Game Boy, with color palettes and tighter portable action.
gba: Game Boy Advance (2001). 32-bit handheld; Golden Sun, Metroid Fusion, and SNES-class portables.
nds: Nintendo DS. Dual screens and a touch stylus — Animal Crossing, Mario Kart DS, and a huge downloadable library.
3ds: Nintendo 3DS. Stereoscopic 3D handheld; needs a standalone core (Tico Azahar) on Switch.
gc: Nintendo GameCube. Compact discs, WaveBird, and GameCube / early Wii-era Nintendo third parties. Standalone Tico Dolphin.
wii: Nintendo Wii. Motion controls and a huge retail + Virtual Console catalog. Standalone Tico Dolphin.
mastersystem: Sega Master System / Mark III. 8-bit Sega counterpart to the NES, strong in Europe and Brazil.
gamegear: Sega Game Gear. Color handheld based on Master System hardware, with a backlit screen.
megadrive: Sega Mega Drive / Genesis. Blast processing 16-bit era — Sonic, Streets of Rage, and sports hits.
saturn: Sega Saturn. Dual-CPU 2D powerhouse and early 3D; a demanding, collector-heavy library.
dreamcast: Sega Dreamcast (1999). Online-ready last Sega home console — Shenmue, Crazy Taxi, NAOMI ports.
psx: Sony PlayStation. CD-based 3D, FMV, and the 32-bit software catalog that remade console gaming.
psp: PlayStation Portable. UMD handheld with PS1 classics, original Sony games, and homebrew-friendly media.
pce: PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16. HuCard and CD add-on from Hudson/NEC — shooters, RPGs, and arcade conversions.
zxspectrum: Sinclair ZX Spectrum. British 8-bit microcomputer: rubber keys, loading tones, and a vast tape library.
